findings.title: retryCount cleanup deletes every method, including already scheduled reminders
findings.body: deleteMany's second OR branch matches only retryCount > 1 and does not constrain method to SMS or scheduled to false. WorkflowReminder is shared by EMAIL and WHATSAPP as well as SMS, and a row can be scheduled: true with a Twilio referenceId while still having retryCount > 1 (a later failed attempt only writes retryCount). The next cron run therefore permanently deletes those rows. Already-queued SMS can no longer be cancelled or reconciled, and any non-SMS reminder that ever exceeds one retry is removed even though this job is only supposed to drop failed SMS reminders.

findings.title: retryCount is a lost-update read-modify-write
findings.body: Both failure paths set retryCount to the value loaded at the start of the loop (reminder.retryCount + 1) instead of an atomic increment. Overlapping cron runs that both read the same count and both fail write the same number back, so the counter can stay at 1 forever. Those reminders are never deleted by the retryCount > 1 cleanup and are rescheduled on every run until scheduledDate passes — the leak this PR is meant to stop. The same non-atomic update in the catch block is unguarded; if a concurrent run already deleted the row, Prisma throws and the exception leaves the for-loop, so the handler 500s and skips every remaining reminder in the batch.

findings.title: Missing number or empty body never counts as a failed attempt
findings.body: retryCount is only increased when scheduleSMS returns falsy or throws. If sendTo is missing or the rendered message is empty, the loop neither schedules nor increments and leaves scheduled false. The next cron selects the same row again, so those reminders are retried until scheduledDate is in the past. That is the same unbounded reschedule the PR describes, and it is not covered by the new retry limit.

findings.title: No test for retry limit or the widened delete
findings.body: The cron now deletes workflow reminders and gives up after two scheduling failures, but the PR adds no test for the retryCount > 1 predicate, the method/scheduled scope of that delete, or the increment on a falsy scheduleSMS result versus a missing sendTo. A wrong OR (as written) silently drops live reminders and would not be caught before merge.
